tei:div.tei:p: We seek thee early, thou who formest the mountains, and declarest unto man what is his thought and secret speech. We pray to thee in shame and confusion, and enumerate our sins to-day. We, both the old and the young, assemble in the houses of prayer, our minor temples; we are enfeebled in strength, our limbs tremble, we are alarmed and terrified on all sides. We dread and fear the two executioners,The Hebrew word is of Greek origin. “anger and fury,”In allusion to a passage in the מדרש where Anger and Fury are represented as two dreadful executioners, appointed by the Almighty to carry out his judgments. those two accusers. When we consider our deeds, and see how abominable they are, tremor, pangs and sorrows take hold of us. Our faces are blackened, and we go about mourning; we are moved exceedingly, and are shaken to pieces; our loins tremble as with the pangs of a woman that travaileth, we are afraid by reason of our numerous sins. Let us therefore replace by our words the offering of the calves, relying on, confiding and hoping in thy mercy.
